Watcom shadow-pointer walk — `vertex_normals` self-updates via array-decay of a sibling array field whose byte offset equals the element stride. Replace `vertex_normals->some_field[0]` reads with direct indexing on the original pointer; drop the shadow init and self-update.

Ghidra pre-increment-array-walk loop artifact on `iVar13` (per-iteration advance via struct-field/pointer arithmetic — single-var `iVar13 = iVar13;` self-assign or two-var `tmp = &iVar13->field; iVar13 = tmp;` ping-pong — plus a constant-index store on `iVar13`). The stride/sentinel are baked from the original struct layout, so it overruns on any layout change (e.g. the 64-bit port). Always wrong as-decoded; cross-reference .asm and rewrite as a straightforward for-loop in a .keep (watch for the skip-row store-offset bug).

resolved_suspects.description: mem* byte count hardcodes an element stride (vertex_count * 0xc) instead of count * sizeof(*dst). If the array holds pointers this corrupts it on the 64-bit build (a *4 moves half of each 8-byte pointer); for value arrays use sizeof for self-documentation.
